reflection.text:
We predicted Actin disruptors (p=0.65) for unblinded bryostatin, whose curated truth is Kinase inhibitors as a protein kinase C modulator (PMID 39772770). The call was driven by extreme high-dose actin texture (act_glcm_contrast z=+29.0, act_std z=+16.3 at 10 uM) plus microscopist stellate/spiky actin and 3/10 atlas neighbors as Actin disruptors.

What misled us was acquisition and weighting: we acquired only two high-dose wells (1 uM and 10 uM, single replicates) where cytoskeletal collapse saturates, so downstream actin remodeling dominated over primary signaling. We over-weighted act_glcm_contrast over the discordant nuclear signal (nuc_dna_mean z=-7.8, nuc_eccentricity z=-7.6 at 1 uM) and discounted the mixed atlas itself — Eg5 3/10 and Protein degradation 2/10 with top hit Protein degradation — which was a flag for a non-actin mechanism.

In retrospect the Protein degradation neighbors fit bryostatin-1 modulation of proteasome function via PKC activation (PMID 29693282) and PKC-epsilon activation by bryostatin-1 (PMID 37629005), but our reference atlas lacks a PKC-modulator class so the kinase signal had no good match. Lesson: with extreme actin/tubulin co-elevation and low-DNA large nuclei, retain upstream kinase signaling and acquire a low-dose titration before committing to a direct cytoskeletal MoA.

## PI review

Verdict: approve.

Top call is justified: actin texture dominates at both doses (act_glcm z=+5.1 at 1µM, +29.0 at 10µM vs tub_glcm +1.7/+10.6; tubulin network still intact at 1µM), with stellate/spiky actin phenotype; flat mitotic-like fraction argues against Aurora/Eg5 despite large nuclei. Mixed atlas (Actin 3/10 but top hit Protein degradation) and single replicates explain the modest 0.65, which is calibrated. No single named step would plausibly overturn this.

## Unblinding

Compound: **bryostatin** (PubChem CID [6435419](https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/6435419))

Identity check: name and BBBC021 structure agree

ChEMBL mechanisms: no curated mechanism in ChEMBL

## Verdict (computed by code)

Incorrect: agent said **Actin disruptors**, BBBC021 annotates **Kinase inhibitors**.

## Reflection

We predicted Actin disruptors (p=0.65) for unblinded bryostatin, whose curated truth is Kinase inhibitors as a protein kinase C modulator (PMID 39772770). The call was driven by extreme high-dose actin texture (act_glcm_contrast z=+29.0, act_std z=+16.3 at 10 uM) plus microscopist stellate/spiky actin and 3/10 atlas neighbors as Actin disruptors.

What misled us was acquisition and weighting: we acquired only two high-dose wells (1 uM and 10 uM, single replicates) where cytoskeletal collapse saturates, so downstream actin remodeling dominated over primary signaling. We over-weighted act_glcm_contrast over the discordant nuclear signal (nuc_dna_mean z=-7.8, nuc_eccentricity z=-7.6 at 1 uM) and discounted the mixed atlas itself — Eg5 3/10 and Protein degradation 2/10 with top hit Protein degradation — which was a flag for a non-actin mechanism.

In retrospect the Protein degradation neighbors fit bryostatin-1 modulation of proteasome function via PKC activation (PMID 29693282) and PKC-epsilon activation by bryostatin-1 (PMID 37629005), but our reference atlas lacks a PKC-modulator class so the kinase signal had no good match. Lesson: with extreme actin/tubulin co-elevation and low-DNA large nuclei, retain upstream kinase signaling and acquire a low-dose titration before committing to a direct cytoskeletal MoA.

What was right:
- Detected strong cytoskeletal remodeling with actin texture dominating tubulin (act_glcm +29.0 vs tub_glcm +10.6 at 10 uM) and lower density visually.
- Recorded an atypical nuclear phenotype (nuc_dna_mean z=-7.8) and mixed atlas (Actin 3/10, Eg5 3/10, Protein degradation 2/10) rather than a clean single-class match, kept probability modest at 0.65.

What was wrong or missed:
- Interpreted downstream actin remodeling as direct Actin disruptor MoA, missing bryostatin PKC-modulator kinase activity.
- Acquired only 1 uM and 10 uM single replicates, so saturating toxicity masked dose-dependent kinase signaling and prevented replicate validation.
- Discounted contradicting evidence: mixed atlas with top hit Protein degradation and Eg5/Aurora visual candidates plus very low DNA content argued against a pure actin mechanism.

Proposed next experiment: Run low-dose bryostatin vs phorbol ester PMA dose-response with PKC membrane-translocation and phospho-PKC-substrate readouts +/- a broad PKC inhibitor, paired with phalloidin F-actin imaging and a cell-free actin polymerization assay to test whether the actin texture is downstream of PKC signaling rather than direct actin disruption.
